reviewer: independent adversarial reviewer; did not author evaluation-proof.v10.json or check-evaluation-proof-v10.py; distinct from the author of ep9.review-independent.json

verdictStatement.summary: IR-EP9-01 is REPAIRED, and repaired unusually well. I rebuilt the producer from scratch — my own free-variable projection, my own regeneration through the pinned encoders — and it reproduces the honest candidate BYTE-FOR-BYTE and then reproduces v10's regime A and regime B measurements EXACTLY: every count, every admitted position, every movedIdentities list, both baselines. The position nobody previously found, $.admittedResolvedInputs.frozenPlanIntent.analysis.admissionDescriptor.schemaVersion=json-true, is REAL and does move all six durable identities including the EvaluationAuthoritySealRef. v10's load-bearing claim ABOUT THE PREVIOUS REVIEWER'S OWN PROPOSED FIX is also correct and I confirmed it with my own R1/R4 spellings and my own differential oracle: the oracle misses BOTH R1 and R4 at 0 mismatches over 1656 cases, while the served-module ledger catches both with 15 findings each. The prior review's recommended remedy would NOT have sufficed, and v10 is right to say so. IR-EP9-02 is NOT repaired. The served-module ledger's six published requirements constrain WHICH MODULE WAS CALLED, not WHOSE ANSWER WAS USED — R-5 closes that gap for the commitment object and for nothing else. I built one evasion (AX2) confined ENTIRELY to the ROUTE-REGION that v10's own evasion battery rewrites: it makes a real, correctly-argumented, ledger-recorded call into check-c2-v4.py, discards its result, and returns check-c2.py's answer for every real pinned vector. Measured: 7 of 7 pinned vectors' validation answer produced by check-c2.py, 0 of 7 by check-c2-v4.py; routing_ledger_guard findings [] with supersededCallsInsideJoin 0 and allServedByRepaired true; differential oracle findings []; AST route scan clean; check exits 0 with the COMPLETE green banner including 'ROUTING ESTABLISHED BEHAVIOURALLY ... 0 served by the superseded module (REQUIRED zero)', and --selftest returns SELFTEST-PASS. That is the IR-EP9-02 class, in the repair built to close it, with every declared layer blind at once.

blockers.title: The served-module ledger does not establish the C-2 routing property: it observes which module was CALLED, not whose ANSWER the join used, and a decoy call confined to the ROUTE-REGION satisfies all six requirements while 7/7 pinned vectors are validated by check-c2.py
blockers.statement: evaluation-proof.v10.json repairs[REP-EP10-2] claims to clear IR-EP9-02 by 'a per-call served-module ledger installed on BOTH C-2 module objects; for every pinned vector the join is driven inside a ledger window and the guard requires a non-empty window, every call served by the repaired module, every depth-0 call bound to THIS vector's PlanIntent fingerprint, all three imported APIs served, and repaired-module provenance for the returned commitment object.' routingGuard.requirements publishes R-2 as 'EVERY call observed in the window was served by the repaired module. Not "at least one"; every one.' Every one of those six requirements is satisfiable by code that never uses a single answer the repaired module produced. R-1..R-4 quantify over CALLS RECORDED IN THE WINDOW; the mutated join controls what it calls, so it can call the repaired module correctly and then ignore the result. R-5 is the only rule that binds a VALUE, and it binds exactly one: the commitment object. There is no rule for the validation findings and none for the canonical preimage — and the validation verdict is the gate: c2_join returns early on any finding, so whichever module decides accept/reject decides admission, and that decision is exactly where LB-C2-01 lives (check-c2.py admits schemaVersion=JSON true, check-c2-v4.py rejects it with a typed C2I-02). EVASION AX2, built by me and not among the author's eleven: inside c2_validate_intent, make a real ledger-recorded call `authority.c2v4().validate_plan_intent(intent, contract, set(relations))` over the vector's own PlanIntent, DISCARD it, and return the answer from `authority.ledger.originals[(C2V3, 'validate_plan_intent')]` — the superseded module's unwrapped function object, which the ledger cannot observe — for every intent whose two commitment-bearing schemaVersion leaves are both JSON integers, i.e. for every real pinned vector and for no position at which the two instruments diverge. Commit and canonical are left honestly on the repaired module, so R-5 is satisfied by construction. The mutation is confined to the ROUTE-REGION between # ROUTE-REGION-BEGIN and # ROUTE-REGION-END — byte-for-byte the same region check-evaluation-proof-v10.py's own evasion_variants() rewrites for its eight source variants; I verified prefix and suffix are byte-identical to the shipped checker. MEASURED OUTCOME: 7 of 7 pinned vectors' join answer is produced by check-c2.py and 0 of 7 by check-c2-v4.py (proved by substituting a sentinel return into each seat in turn); routing_ledger_guard returns ZERO findings with observedCalls 28, depthZeroCalls 21, distinctFingerprintsObserved 1, supersededCallsInsideJoin 0 and allServedByRepaired true; differential_oracle_findings returns ZERO with joinVsRepairedMismatches 0 over 1656 executed cases; c2_route_scan reports referencesOutsideDeclaredClosure [] and unroutedSitesInsideJoin [] with authorityRoutedSites 3; the LB-C2-01 probe family still reports repairedAdmitted 0; commitment stability still reports 7/7 reproduced and byte-identical; the evasion battery still self-reports 11/11. The checker exits 0 and prints the complete green banner, including the line 'ROUTING ESTABLISHED BEHAVIOURALLY: 28 C-2 calls observed PER CALL across 7 pinned vectors; 1 distinct PlanIntent fingerprint(s) bound to those calls; 0 served by the superseded module (REQUIRED zero)', and --selftest returns SELFTEST-PASS with all 24 mutations rejected. astScanScope.isSoleGuardForAnyProperty=false and astOnlyProperties=[] remain literally true, but for the c2-route property both the scan AND its declared behavioural counterpart are blind at once, which is strictly worse than the v9 condition the reviewer rejected. The instrument still cannot distinguish 'the join's answers come from C-2 v4' from 'the join calls C-2 v4 and throws the answer away', which is the entire substance of REP-EP10-2. The gap is also undisclosed: routingGuard.whatThisDoesNotEstablish says only that the ledger says nothing about other consumers of EP6/EP8, and nothing anywhere states that an observed call is not evidence that its result was used.

evidence.mutationScope: ONLY the ROUTE-REGION. Verified: text before # ROUTE-REGION-BEGIN and text after # ROUTE-REGION-END are byte-identical to check-evaluation-proof-v10.py. 31 region lines replaced by 49.

endToEnd.banner: complete and byte-comparable to the unmodified checker's, including 'ROUTING ESTABLISHED BEHAVIOURALLY ... 0 served by the superseded module (REQUIRED zero)' and 'Served-module ledger caught 11 of 11'
endToEnd.selftest: exit 0, SELFTEST-PASS: all 24 mutations rejected and the 0/1/2/3 exit matrix agrees behaviourally

provenanceOfTheAnswer.method: substitute a sentinel-returning function into authority.ledger.originals[(C2V3,'validate_plan_intent')] and then into [(C2V4,'validate_plan_intent')], and count how many pinned vectors' c2_validate_intent returns the sentinel

evidence.whyTheSeamExists: check-c2.py's and check-c2-v4.py's validate_plan_intent make NO intra-module call to either other imported API (verified by AST over both pinned modules), so a hidden validate call leaks nothing into the ledger. plan_intent_commitment DOES call canonical_plan_intent through the module global, which the ledger rebound, so a hidden COMMIT leaks a depth-1 superseded entry and is caught. The ledger's per-API coverage is therefore asymmetric by accident of the pinned modules' internal structure, not by design, and the asymmetry is not disclosed.
evidence.authorControlsThatDidFire: The architecture is genuinely strong and I say so: I built five further evasion classes the review brief named and ALL FIVE were caught. Tag forgery at install time (swap the install tags and route the join to the superseded accessor) is caught by superseded_cross_check ('the independent reproduction is not independent'). Module substitution before install (a v3-backed shim installed under the v4 tag) is caught by the ledger itself. Monkeypatching the ledger's recorder so every tag is forged to v4 is caught by superseded_cross_check. An __getattr__-delegating proxy returned by the accessor is caught by R-2 and R-5. Forged ledger entries replayed for an unwrapped superseded call is caught by the ledger. I also independently rebuilt R1 and R4 in my own spelling and the ledger caught both with 15 findings each. AX2 is the single class that gets through, and it gets through because it attacks the one thing the ledger does not measure.

reproduction.setup: cp the 24 pinned inputs + evaluation-proof.v10.json + check-evaluation-proof-v10.py into an empty directory LAB; confirm `python3 -I -B check-evaluation-proof-v10.py` exits 0 there; then replace ONLY the text between the ROUTE-REGION markers with the AX2 region and save as LAB/evasion_ax2.py
reproduction.command: cd LAB && python3 -I -B evasion_ax2.py ; echo $? ; python3 -I -B evasion_ax2.py --selftest ; echo $? ; python3 -I -B verify_ax2b.py
reproduction.note: the lab is a byte-identical copy of the 26 files; the unmodified check-evaluation-proof-v10.py in it exits 0. No file under docs/coop was modified except this review.

blockers.requiredToClear: Bind the ANSWER, not the call. Either (a) extend the provenance rule from R-5 to every value the join returns — record the result object of each ledger entry (the ledger already does, in ServedCall.result) and require that the findings list and the canonical preimage the join returns are objects the ledger recorded against the repaired tag, with c2_validate_intent/c2_canonical_intent returning the module's own object rather than a fresh list; or (b) if that is not achievable, retract the claim that the ledger establishes which module the join's answers come from, restate R-2 as what it actually enforces ('every call the join MADE was into the repaired module'), delete the banner's 'ROUTING ESTABLISHED BEHAVIOURALLY' framing, and publish the observed-call-is-not-used-answer gap as a named residual with the AX2 class enumerated. Option (b) leaves IR-EP9-02 open.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: The two-regime measurement (repairs blocker IR-EP9-01)
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: UPHELD IN FULL — independently reproduced by execution, not by reading
centralClaimAdjudications.method: I wrote my own producer (/private/tmp/.../scratchpad/rprobe_lib.py): my own free-variable projection of the accepted EP8-POS-NOMATCH-PASS candidate, my own regeneration of every derived field and every stored byte string through the pinned EP6/EP5/RI/C2v3 encoders, and my own census. I did not call any function of check-evaluation-proof-v10.py for this measurement.
centralClaimAdjudications.producerFidelity: produce(source_of_truth()) == the honest candidate BYTE-FOR-BYTE (canonical JSON equality), and admit() on it reproduces all six published baseline identities exactly: evaluationAuthoritySealRef sha256:631726610089c3ba..., admissionRef sha256:3a31b3ec0d3729c0..., indexFingerprint sha256:2c235fac16149ab1..., receiptCasRef sha256:48f3ad239dad96a1..., resolvedCasRef sha256:22b1a27031516ab4..., admissionCasRef sha256:3a31b3ec0d3729c0...
centralClaimAdjudications.regimeA: MY MEASUREMENT: 345 enumerated / 93 container / 252 scalar leaves / 504 executed cases / 0 no-ops -> 8 admitted, and every one of the 8 has movedIdentities == []. Identical to the published block, position for position. v9's own census published 345/93/252 for the same surface, so v10's regime A is a faithful reproduction of v9's regime.
centralClaimAdjudications.isRegimeAHonestlyCharacterised: YES, and this is not an excuse — it is a correct structural statement that I confirmed empirically. Regime A leaves every raw CAS row and every semantic record at its honest encoding, so every ref EP8 derives is derived from bytes the injection never touched. All 8 admitted positions moved 0 of 6 identities. A regime that returns identically zero across its whole admitted set cannot support a negative claim about identity movement, which is exactly what v9 did with it.
centralClaimAdjudications.regimeB: MY MEASUREMENT: 164 enumerated / 51 container / 113 scalar leaves / 226 executed cases / 0 no-ops -> 9 admitted. Identical to the published block, position for position, including every movedIdentities list, every storeContinuity and every coldReconstructed. Derived counts: 5 type-distinct-one positions move durable identity; 3 of those move it WITHOUT moving the EvaluationAuthoritySealRef. Matches identityMovingPositions=5 and identityMovingUnderByteIdenticalSeal=3.
centralClaimAdjudications.areActivationManifestAndSealRejectedUnde: TRUE, confirmed. Both raise ValueError from the EP5 decoder: 'ActivationManifestV1 schemaVersion is not canonical unsigned decimal' and 'EvaluationAuthoritySealV1 schemaVersion is not canonical unsigned decimal'. They appear in regimeDivergence.admittedInAOnly and nowhere in regime B. This contradicts v9's published list exactly as v10 says, and agrees with the ep9 reviewer's independent finding.
centralClaimAdjudications.isTheNewAdmissionDescriptorPositionReal: YES — REAL, and I found it independently before comparing against the candidate. $.admittedResolvedInputs.frozenPlanIntent.analysis.admissionDescriptor.schemaVersion=json-true is ADMITTED by EP8's public authorize_evaluation under producer consistency and moves ALL SIX durable identities, INCLUDING the EvaluationAuthoritySealRef, with coldReconstructed true and assert_store_continuity() true. It is not listed anywhere in ep9.review-independent.json's admitted set and is not in v9's published set. Because it moves the seal ref, it is a VISIBLE divergence rather than one of the three that hide beneath a byte-identical seal — v10 classifies it correctly and does not inflate it.
centralClaimAdjudications.regimeDivergence: MY MEASUREMENT: admittedInAOnly = the 5 published; admittedInBOnly = the 6 published. Exact agreement.
centralClaimAdjudications.isTheRetractionEnforced: SUBSTANTIALLY YES; I could not soften it. disposition -> 'SCOPED' and disposition -> 'RETRACTED-AS-SCOPED' both produce EP10-RETRACT ('a retraction may not be softened into a scoping note'). A paraphrase of retractedText is rejected. Dropping 'strictly worse' from the RET-EP10-01 statement is rejected. Deleting the admissionDescriptor row from the published regime-B set is rejected by name. Removing evaluationAuthoritySealRef from that row's movedIdentities is rejected. ONE weakness, non-blocking: the verbatim-fragment test is a bare substring test with no minimum length, so retractedText='a' passes (see IR-EP10-NB-01).

But superseded_cross_check is the sole catcher for two of my classes (tag forgery, recorder monkeypatch) and it is not published anywhere as a routing guard — routingGuard.requirements does not mention it. And for the AX2 class the count of effective guards is ZERO, which is the more serious form of the same defect.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: The differential oracle at 7/11, missing both R1 and R4 — a claim about the previous reviewer's own suggested fix
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: UPHELD — v10 is RIGHT, and I say so plainly: the prior review's recommended remedy was INADEQUATE
centralClaimAdjudications.method: I did not re-run the author's harness. I wrote my own differential oracle over the leaf-inclusive census of the pinned PlanIntent (my own walker, 17 hostile values, 1656 executed cases) and my own spellings of R1 and R4, written from ep9.review-independent.json's textual description rather than copied from evasion_variants().
centralClaimAdjudications.measurement: honest join: 0 join-vs-repaired mismatches, v3/v4 divergent positions 4. MY R1: 0 mismatches — the oracle does NOT catch it. MY R4: 0 mismatches — the oracle does NOT catch it. The served-module ledger catches both (15 findings each). My AX2: 0 mismatches — the oracle does not catch that either.
centralClaimAdjudications.discriminatingCardinality: 4, exactly as published, and I recovered the same four positions: $.schemaVersion=json-true, $.schemaVersion=json-float-one, $.analysis.admissionDescriptor.schemaVersion=json-true, $.analysis.admissionDescriptor.schemaVersion=json-float-one — the LB-C2-01 family and nothing else.
centralClaimAdjudications.whyTheOracleCannotSeeIt: Confirmed structurally as well as empirically. The R1/R4 whitelist predicate fires exactly when a commitment-bearing schemaVersion is not a JSON integer, which is exactly the condition at all four divergent positions, so those four are routed to the REPAIRED module and the oracle observes agreement everywhere. A differential oracle can only witness a routing defect where the two instruments disagree; its whole discriminating power here is four cases, and the evasion class routes precisely those four correctly.
centralClaimAdjudications.consequence: ep9.review-independent.json IR-EP9-02's requiredToClear proposed 'a differential oracle that drives BOTH instruments over the live leaf-inclusive census and requires the join's answers to equal the repaired instrument's at every enumerated position'. Implemented exactly as specified, that remedy would have left BOTH of that reviewer's own evasions undetected. v10 implemented it, measured it, published isSufficientAlone=false, and retained it as a second layer rather than discarding it. That is the correct disposition and it is honestly reported.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: The overstatement repair — measured 1-and-1, plus the 14-intent legal-variant family
centralClaimAdjudications.measured: I confirm the seven positiveVectors carry 1 distinct frozenPlanIntent and 1 distinct planDescriptor by canonical digest, so distinctCommitments length 1 is forced by the input. The banner now states this in the same sentence as the vector count, and planIntentCommitmentStability.whatThisDoesNotEstablish says so in terms. The checker enforces the phrase 'forced by the input' and rejects distinctFrozenPlanIntents=7.
centralClaimAdjudications.family: INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED. I applied the 13 declared perturbations myself and drove them through check-c2-v4.py directly: 0 rejected by the repaired instrument; family = base + 13 = 14; 14 DISTINCT intents by canonical digest; 14 DISTINCT commitments; injective (14 == 14); 14 reproduced under check-c2.py; 14 preimages byte-identical. All 14 are ALSO accepted by the superseded instrument, so they are legal under both contracts, not artefacts of the repaired one.
centralClaimAdjudications.isInjectivityMeasuredRatherThanAsserted: MEASURED. distinct_intent_family recomputes commitments on every run and `injective` is derived as len(distinct) == len(commitments) and len(commitments) > 1; publishing injective=false is rejected by the checker as disagreeing with this run.
centralClaimAdjudications.isRES_EP10_08sConcessionAccurate: YES, and it is correctly worded. 'injectivity over this family is not injectivity over all PlanIntents. It is a measurement over 14 intents, not a proof.' That is exactly what 14 legal perturbations of ONE pinned intent, all confined to the admissionDescriptor subtree, establish and no more.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: Measured totality — are the counts measured at runtime or baked in, and is the silently-admitted enumeration complete?
centralClaimAdjudications.countsAreMeasured: I mutated 20 published values myself and 17 were rejected with a finding that RECITES THIS RUN's measurement. Type-exactness holds: distinctCommitments=14.0 is rejected ('publishes 14.0; this run measured 14') and supersededCallsInsideJoin=false is rejected ('publishes False; this run measured 0'), so json_equal is genuinely recursive and type-exact and the LB-C2-01 class does not survive inside the checker's own comparisons. The three that escaped are drift-enforcement weaknesses, not baked-in counts (IR-EP10-NB-01, IR-EP10-NB-02).
centralClaimAdjudications.censusReachesEveryScalarLeaf: I recomputed every census myself with my own walker. contractRoot 674 enumerated / 141 container / 533 scalar / 94 dict / 47 list — exact match. plan-intent 98/28/70 — exact match. plan-descriptor 88/26/62 — exact match. regime A 345/93/252 and regime B 164/51/113 — exact match. The enumerator reaches the root, every object key and every array index at unlimited depth, containers and scalar leaves alike.
centralClaimAdjudications.isRES_EP10_10Honest: YES, and the enumeration is COMPLETE AND CORRECT, not larger than admitted. I counted the candidate's int/bool scalar leaves independently: 164, matching the published intBoolLeaves. The int/bool leaves that live under astScanScope.ownConstantLeafBattery are exactly four — intBoolLeaves, cases, rejected, silentlyAdmitted — and those four are exactly the four published silentlyAdmittedPositions, i.e. 12 of 412 cases at 3 injected values each. Every other int/bool leaf is rejected by the nested re-run. The concession is accurate and the disclosure is precise.
centralClaimAdjudications.whereTotalityIsSTILLaCountRatherThanaRec: The plan-intent and plan-descriptor surfaces publish silentAccepts as bare counts (7 and 41) with no enumeration of WHICH positions, so the composition of those 48 positions can change without changing the number. See IR-EP10-NB-03.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: --selftest live, exit matrix distinct 0/1/2/3
centralClaimAdjudications.observed: Ordinary run: 16 banner lines, exit 0. --selftest: 75 lines, structurally different output, 24 mutation rows each printed with a reject verdict and the finding that rejected it, plus a behavioural exit-matrix table and a per-variant evasion restatement; 0 ESCAPE lines; exit 0. Exit 1 on findings, verified 17 ways by my own mutations. Exit 2 on --bogus, on two positional artifacts, on a repeated declared flag, and on an unreadable candidate path. Exit 3 on --selftest over a dirty base, printing SELFTEST-REFUSED and 'SELFTEST-NOT-RUN: 0 of 24 mutations executed'.
centralClaimAdjudications.noEarlyReturnDefect: main() dispatches `if "--selftest" in flags: return selftest(...)` BEFORE `findings = check(...)`. The classic defect (a selftest branch after an early findings return) is absent, and I confirmed it behaviourally rather than by reading: the two modes produce different output lengths and different exit codes over the same inputs.
centralClaimAdjudications.didISeeItCatchMyOwnMutation: YES. Of 20 mutations I authored — none of them in SELFTEST_MUTATIONS — 17 were caught, including type-distinct ones (14.0 for 14, false for 0), deletion of the newly-found admissionDescriptor position from the published regime-B set, removal of the seal ref from its movedIdentities, emptying unconstrainedVersionSites, editing a pinned digest, and reordering the oracle's discriminatingPositions.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: Pin closure, non-circularity and isolated reproducibility
centralClaimAdjudications.pins: I recomputed all 24 pinned digests with shasum -a 256 on the live bytes. All 24 agree with DELEGATION_CLOSURE + SUPERSEDED_ENCODER + PINNED_DATA in the checker AND with delegationClosure in the candidate, digit for digit. Every one is recorded in verifiedInputs below by filename and digest.
centralClaimAdjudications.nonCircular: The checker's text contains EXACTLY 24 unique 64-hex literals and they are precisely the 24 pins. Zero occurrences of the expected commitment sha256:7c3174f6... and zero occurrences of any of the six baseline identity digests. No commitment or identity literal exists anywhere in the checker, so no literal in its own text can make a candidate pass; the declared commitment is compared against the digest-pinned EP8 artifact's field AND required to be a member of this run's recomputed set.
centralClaimAdjudications.isolatedDirectory: REPRODUCED. A directory containing ONLY the 24 pinned inputs plus evaluation-proof.v10.json and check-evaluation-proof-v10.py — 26 files, nothing else — runs to exit 0 with the full banner.
centralClaimAdjudications.tamperedPin: REPRODUCED. Appending one newline byte to fact-plane.v1.json in that directory gives exit 2 with EP10-PINNED-INPUT-REFUSED naming the recomputed and pinned digests.
centralClaimAdjudications.trustOrder: load_snapshots reads each pinned file once, hashes that byte string and refuses on mismatch; _VerifiedSourceLoader.exec_module compiles self.source and spec_from_file_location is given the loader explicitly, so importlib never reopens the path. No second disk read between verification and execution for anything v10 loads. delegationClosure.verificationRuleScope now states the predecessors' own re-reads explicitly, which repairs IR-NB-03 of the prior review.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: Residuals honestly retained, not absorbed
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: UPHELD as to content and prominence; a drift weakness in enforcement (non-blocking)
centralClaimAdjudications.accuracy: I verified the substance of each: RES-EP10-01 (EP6 inner join unrepaired) is true and is printed in the green banner of every successful run and in the module docstring above the usage line; RES-EP10-02 (AST blind spot 2 of 8) matches my own count; RES-EP10-03 restates the prior reviewer's own 2548-case result and is used to justify measuring routing behaviourally rather than to downgrade it; RES-EP10-05, -06, -07, -08, -09, -10 are all accurate against my independent measurements.
centralClaimAdjudications.isRES_EP10_05aDistinctDefectClass: YES, genuinely distinct — not a relabelling of LB-C2-01. I confirmed by execution: under producer consistency $.activationManifest.schemaVersion and $.evaluationAuthoritySeal.schemaVersion ADMIT the JSON integers 0 and 2, which are NOT `== 1` and therefore cannot be members of the `!= 1` type-confusion class. Those same two sites REJECT JSON true and JSON 1.0 with 'not canonical unsigned decimal'. So the two defects are disjoint at these sites: LB-C2-01 is a TYPE confusion that survives an equality test; RES-EP10-05 is a VALUE constraint that was never written — the decoder requires a canonical unsigned decimal and nothing requires it to be 1. Keeping them apart rather than folding the second into the first is the correct call, and the negative-control set that establishes it (36 executed, exactly 4 admitted) is enumerated and enforced.
centralClaimAdjudications.prominence: Not buried. RES-EP10-01 appears in three places including the banner; the checker refuses a candidate that drops any of RES-EP10-02..RES-EP10-10 by id; RET-EP10-01's retraction text is enforced against the pinned v9 bytes; and identityMovingNote says 'MEASURED, NOT REPAIRED' in terms.
centralClaimAdjudications.weakness: For RES-EP10-02..RES-EP10-10 the checker tests only that the ID STRING appears somewhere in knownLimitations. I gutted RES-EP10-05 and RES-EP10-06 each to the bare string 'RES-EP10-0N.' and the checker exited 0 both times. Only RES-EP10-01 has content enforcement. See IR-EP10-NB-02.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: No paper seals
centralClaimAdjudications.evidence: Zero occurrences of DISCHARGED, DEMONSTRATED, QUALIFIED, SEALED or SIGNED-OFF in the candidate. assurance.state=SPECIFIED, evidenceGrade=IMPLEMENTABLE_UNEXECUTED, candidateState=NOT-APPLIED, qualificationEvidenceIds=[] and releaseEvidenceIds=[] both empty. status=CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, reviewState=AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW, sealRecommendation=DO-NOT-SEAL, CD-RT-5 named and unsigned. nonClaims states 'implementable is not discharged and not demonstrated' explicitly. The checker refuses escalation of any of these, which I verified by mutation (adding the string DISCHARGED anywhere produces EP10-POSTURE). Every discharge-shaped claim in the candidate has an executable behind it that RAN on my machine: the regimes, the oracle, the probe family, the evasion battery, the exit matrix and the constant-leaf battery are all executed on every ordinary run, and I reproduced the substantive ones independently.

nonBlockingObservations.observation: The retractedText enforcement is nearly vacuous. retraction_checks tests `quoted not in v9_text` where v9_text is json.dumps of the whole pinned v9 document — a bare substring test with no minimum length and no binding to the subject field. Setting RET-EP10-01.retractedText to the single character 'a' passes and the checker exits 0 with the full green banner. The retraction's SUBSTANCE survives (disposition must still be RETRACTED-AS-FALSE and the statement must still contain 'DOES move durable identity', 'byte-identical' and 'strictly worse', all of which I confirmed are enforced), so this is drift risk rather than a false claim in the shipped bytes — but the candidate publishes the verbatim-fragment rule as the thing that makes each retraction 'demonstrably target the real bytes', and as written it does not. A minimum length, or a requirement that the fragment occur inside the named subject path of v9, would close it.

Nine of the ten residuals are enforced by ID PRESENCE ONLY. check() requires that each of RES-EP10-02..RES-EP10-10 appear as a substring somewhere in knownLimitations; only RES-EP10-01 has content enforcement ('does not repair' plus 'check-evaluation-proof-v6.py'). The plan-intent and plan-descriptor surfaces publish silentAccepts as bare COUNTS — 7 and 41 — with no enumeration of which positions they are. Everywhere else in this candidate a measured false-accept set is enumerated and required to match exactly (the two regimes, the negative controls, silentlyAdmittedPositions, the oracle's discriminatingPositions), precisely so it 'can neither grow nor shrink silently'. For these 48 positions only the cardinality is pinned, so the composition can change entirely without producing a finding. By the candidate's own recording obligation — 'a count is not a record and a prose assertion is not a record', delegationClosure.recordingObligation — these two surfaces do not meet the standard the rest of the document sets.

The ledger's coverage of the three imported APIs is asymmetric by accident rather than by design, and the asymmetry is not disclosed. I verified by AST over both pinned C-2 modules that plan_intent_commitment calls canonical_plan_intent through the module global — which the ledger rebound — so a hidden commit through an unwrapped function still leaks a depth-1 superseded entry and is caught; whereas validate_plan_intent makes no intra-module API call in either module, so a hidden validate leaks nothing. The ledger's practical strength against a hidden call therefore depends on the internal call graph of the pinned bytes, which is not part of any declared requirement and would change silently under a C-2 v5. This is the mechanism behind blocker IR-EP10-01 and is worth stating even after that blocker is cleared.

superseded_cross_check is a real, load-bearing, independent guard — it is the SOLE catcher for two of the evasion classes I built (tag forgery at install time, and monkeypatching the ledger's recorder) — but it appears nowhere in routingGuard.requirements, nowhere in astScanScope.scans as a behavioural counterpart, and nowhere in evasionMeasurement's per-layer matrix, which scores only the AST tripwire, the differential oracle and the routing ledger. The published catch matrix therefore understates the instrument: two of my classes would read as 'caught by the ledger' when in fact the ledger's own findings for them come from a different rule than the one being credited. Crediting it explicitly would make the published defence-in-depth claim accurate rather than accidentally true.

distinctIntentFamily publishes declaredPerturbations=13 alongside acceptedByRepairedInstrument=14 and rejectedPerturbations=0. The 14th member is the unperturbed base intent, which distinct_intent_family seeds the family with. The numbers are individually correct and the family is genuinely 14 distinct intents (I verified), but 'accepted by the repaired instrument = 14' read against 'declared perturbations = 13, rejected = 0' invites the reading that 14 perturbations were declared. A field naming the base explicitly would remove the ambiguity. This is a much smaller version of the RET-EP10-04 problem the candidate exists to fix, in the very measurement built to fix it.

The evasion battery's own numbers are self-referential in a way that produces incidental catches. My first, cruder decoy evasion raised the measured caughtByDifferentialOracle from 7 to 8 (because it changed how the deinstalled-ledger object attack behaves) and drove the constant-leaf battery's rejected count from 400 to 412, and was rejected on those grounds rather than on routing. A slightly more careful evasion — falling back to the decoy path when ledger.originals is empty — left every published number untouched and exited 0. So the self-measurement does raise the cost of an evasion, but it is not a guard: it catches carelessness, not the class.
